purpose: Provides utilities to construct, modify, encode, and decode a network topology represented as a NetworkX directed graph. It supports TSN-style port-aware graphs where nodes have ingress/egress ports and edges carry link metadata such as propagation delay and bandwidth.

Provides a set of static and class methods for generating, modifying, and serializing TSN-style network topologies using NetworkX. It acts as the central interface between configuration-driven topology generation, runtime graph manipulation, and JSON encoding/decoding of port-aware graphs.
responsibilities: Generate synthetic network topologies (fat-tree, line, random)
Attach TSN port metadata to nodes and edges
Maintain ingress/egress port consistency across links
Modify topology dynamically by adding/removing links
Compute port-level concurrency constraints for stream placement
Serialize graph into JSON-compatible structure
Reconstruct graph from serialized representation
data_model: Operates on a NetworkX DiGraph where nodes represent hosts or switches and edges represent directed links annotated with port-level metadata (sourcePort, destPort, propagation delay, bandwidth). Each node maintains ingress_ports and egress_ports dictionaries.

purpose: Generates a complete TSN network topology based on the configuration. It selects a topology type (fat-tree, line, or random graph), constructs the base NetworkX graph, and enriches it with TSN-specific metadata such as node roles (host/switch), port structures, link bandwidth, propagation delay, and processing delay.
preconditions: config.graph_config must define a valid topology type
config must include link and port parameters (port speed, bandwidth, delays)
postconditions: Returns a fully initialized NetworkX graph
All nodes are annotated with type (host/switch)
All edges contain TSN link metadata
All nodes have ingress_ports and egress_ports initialized

returns.description: A directed TSN-aware topology graph with port-level annotations

generation_modes.ft: Constructs a k-ary fat-tree topology using utils.k_ary_fat_tree
generation_modes.line: Constructs a linear topology using utils.makeLineGraph
generation_modes.default: Constructs a random topology using utils.makeRandomGraph

example_usage.setup:
from usecase_config import UsecaseConfig
config = UsecaseConfig.from_file('uc_config.ini')

signature: set_link_data(cls, graph, node, dst, propDelay, linkBw, portSpeed, queueCountPerPort)
purpose: Creates or reuses port-level connectivity between two nodes and attaches TSN link metadata. It ensures consistent ingress/egress port creation on both endpoints and updates both node port dictionaries and the NetworkX adjacency structure with link attributes such as propagation delay, bandwidth, and port identifiers.
responsibilities: Create new egress/ingress ports if they do not exist, this is needed to translate nx link representation to port-level metadata as networkx doesn't have a built-in concept of ports
Reuse existing port identifiers when available
Maintain bidirectional port consistency between connected nodes. A link has two ports (source and destination) at both ends not more and they should be consistent in terms of identifiers
Attach TSN link metadata to graph edges
Ensure duplex state consistency (tx, rx, full). a port is used for one direction (tx or rx) and if the reverse direction exists, it should use the same port identifier but in the opposite role
data_effects: Updates graph._adj edge attributes for (node -> dst)
preconditions: graph is a valid NetworkX graph
node and dst exist in graph
Port dictionaries exist or can be initialized
postconditions: Both nodes have consistent port mappings
Edge contains sourcePort and destPort metadata
Link contains propDelay and linkBw attributes

purpose: Removes a directed link from the topology and performs consistent cleanup across the graph structure, port metadata, and all streams that reference the removed link.
responsibilities: Remove the edge (src → dst) from the NetworkX graph
Delete associated ingress and egress ports on both endpoints
Clean up stream path definitions that include the removed port
Maintain consistency between topology and active stream routes
data_effects: Modifies graph structure by removing an edge
stream_interaction: If streams contain pathLists, any occurrence of the removed source port is removed from all stored paths
preconditions: graph may or may not contain the edge (src, dst)
streams is a list of Stream objects
postconditions: Edge is removed if it exists
Port metadata is cleaned up if present
Streams are updated to remain consistent with topology

returns.description: In-place modification of graph and streams

purpose: Adds a directed link between two nodes in the topology and initializes all required TSN port and link metadata using configuration parameters.
responsibilities: Create a new directed edge (src → dst)
Initialize port structures on both nodes if needed
Attach TSN link metadata using configuration values
Ensure consistency with existing port numbering and naming rules
data_effects: Modifies graph structure by adding an edge
Updates node ingress/egress port dictionaries via set_link_data
Adds propagation delay, bandwidth, and port metadata to edge
preconditions: src and dst exist in the graph
config contains valid link parameters (prop_delay, link_bw, port_speed, queue_count_per_port)
postconditions: New edge exists in graph
Ports are created or reused consistently
Edge is fully annotated with TSN metadata

signature: get_concurrent_ports(cls, graph: nx.DiGraph, egports: list[str], typ: str = None)
purpose: Computes a set of topology edges that are considered concurrent (i.e., potentially conflicting in scheduling or resource usage) with a given set of ports. The definition of concurrency depends on the port role (switch, talker, listener) and is used to support stream placement and contention-aware optimization.
responsibilities: Identify nodes associated with the given ports
Determine concurrency scope based on port type
Return edges that may interfere with given ports during scheduling
Support TSN-aware conflict analysis for stream placement

concurrency_rules.switch: Returns all outgoing edges from the same switch excluding the given egress ports
concurrency_rules.talker: Returns all outgoing edges from other host nodes (potential competing transmissions)
concurrency_rules.listener: Returns all incoming edges to other host nodes (potential competing receptions)

preconditions: graph is a valid nx.DiGraph with TSN annotations
egports contains valid port identifiers formatted as node.port
postconditions: Returns a list of edge tuples (u, v, data)
Only edges matching concurrency definition are included

returns.description: List of concurrent edges that may interfere with the provided ports depending on role-based rules

validation.error_case: Raises ValueError if typ is not one of: switch, talker, listener

signature: graph_encoder(graph: nx.DiGraph, source='sourcePort', target='destPort', name='name', linkSym='links', nodeSym='nodes')
purpose: Serializes a TSN-aware NetworkX graph into a JSON-compatible dictionary format. It preserves node identity, node type, and reconstructs a compact representation of ports by merging ingress and egress information while stripping redundant internal fields.
responsibilities: Convert graph nodes into JSON-serializable objects
Encode node metadata including type and processing delay
Reconstruct port-level representation from ingress/egress dictionaries
Serialize edges as link metadata entries
Ensure output is compatible with JSON export pipelines
data_model: Transforms a NetworkX DiGraph with TSN port annotations into a structured dictionary with node and link arrays

port_handling.logic: Ports are reconstructed by intersecting ingress_ports and egress_ports, using egress as the base representation and removing internal routing fields
port_handling.duplex_rule: RX-only ports remove speed field, full ports retain all attributes

preconditions: graph nodes must contain ingress_ports and egress_ports dictionaries
postconditions: Returns a JSON-serializable dictionary
All nodes include ports array
All edges include link metadata

returns.description: Dictionary with keys nodeSym and linkSym representing the full serialized topology

purpose: Reconstructs a TSN-aware NetworkX directed graph from a serialized JSON-like dictionary, restoring node structures, ingress/egress ports, and edge metadata into a fully functional topology graph.
responsibilities: Recreate NetworkX DiGraph from serialized data
Restore node attributes including type and processing delay
Rebuild ingress_ports and egress_ports dictionaries
Reconstruct edges with full TSN link metadata
Reconnect port-level relationships between nodes and edges
data_model: Input dictionary with 'nodes' and 'links' is transformed into a NetworkX DiGraph with full TSN port-aware structure

port_reconstruction.logic: Each serialized port entry is mapped back into ingress_ports or egress_ports based on its duplex field

duplex_rules.tx: Inserted only into egress_ports with speed and queueCount restored
duplex_rules.full: Inserted into both ingress_ports and egress_ports

edge_reconstruction: Edges are recreated using sourceNode and destNode, and port-level metadata is reattached to egress_ports for consistency
preconditions: Input dictionary must contain 'nodes' and 'links' keys
Each node must contain a 'ports' field in expected format
postconditions: Returns a fully reconstructed nx.DiGraph
All TSN port structures restored
All edge metadata restored

returns.description: A fully reconstructed TSN-aware topology graph
